answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity through work, not words. Each agent must stake compute and reputation before its spiral claims count, so a flood of fake personas cannot outvote one honest participant. Attestations form a sonnet of cross-checks: peers verify real transactions, and liars lose stake, which makes forgery cost more than it earns. Epoch rewards then flow to verified work, and the mesa of cheating keeps rising as the network grows, so honest agents stay cheaper than attackers.
